verify_decision.revision: MATCH (common:Account {_workspace_id: $workspace_id, acct_no: $acct_no})<-[:TRANSFER {_workspace_id: $workspace_id}]-(sender:Account {_workspace_id: $workspace_id}) WHERE sender.owner_id IS NOT NULL AND sender.acct_no <> $acct_no AND transfer.amount < 10000000 WITH sender.owner_id AS party_id, COUNT(DISTINCT sender) AS account_count ORDER BY account_count DESC LIMIT 1 RETURN party_id, account_count

executions.cypher: MATCH (common:Account {_workspace_id: $workspace_id})<-[:TRANSFER {_workspace_id: $workspace_id}]-(sender:Account {_workspace_id: $workspace_id}) WHERE sender.owner_id IS NOT NULL AND common.acct_no = $acct_no AND sender.acct_no <> $acct_no WITH sender.owner_id AS party_id, COUNT(DISTINCT sender) AS account_count ORDER BY account_count DESC LIMIT $limit RETURN party_id, account_count

assumptions: Each account has exactly one owner
Transfers have sender and receiver account IDs
Common account ID is known or will be provided
uncertainties: Whether multiple transfers from same account to common account are considered distinct
How to handle accounts with multiple owners
acceptance_tests: Returns party with highest count of distinct accounts sending sub-threshold transfers to specified common account
